Equality or Equity?

A ten-minute walk to school became a lesson in fairness, time and the wisdom that can come from the smallest voices.

Originally published on Substack2 min read
FamilyFairnessLearning

Quick question.

Which is better, equality or equity?

Take a second and pick one.

A few mornings ago, my daughter asked me this while we were walking to school.

Lately life has been quite busy. Between work, the MBA, and everything that comes with building life away from the place we once called home, time feels like it moves very fast.

If I’m honest, one small regret during this MBA journey is that sometimes I feel I don’t spend enough time with my family.

So recently I started doing something simple.

Every morning I walk my daughter to school. It’s about a 10-minute walk, but it has quietly become the best part of my day. No phones, no rush. Just a little time to talk.

One morning she mentioned something interesting from school.

Equality vs. Equity.

So let me ask again.

Which do you think is better?

My first answer was equality.
Everyone gets the same thing. That sounded fair to me.

But my daughter shook her head.

“No,” she said. “Equity is better.”

I asked her why.

She paused for a moment and then said something that stayed with me.

“When it’s equal, it may not be fair.
And when it’s fair, it may not be equal.”

Then she explained it with a simple example.

Imagine a teacher giving the whole class granola bars.

Equality means every student gets the same granola bar.

But what if one student is allergic to nuts?
What if another skipped breakfast and is still hungry?
What if someone already ate?

Giving everyone the same thing looks fair.

But it doesn’t help everyone in the same way.

Equity means giving each student what they actually need.

I smiled because sometimes the most thoughtful ideas come from the smallest voices.

That morning reminded me of two things.

First, fairness is not always about treating everyone the same. Sometimes it is about understanding what people really need.

And second, in the middle of busy work, deadlines, and studying, the most important thing we can give our children is our time.

Sometimes all it takes is a 10-minute walk to school.

And sometimes during that walk, you realize your child might be the one teaching the lesson….
